top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, one writer, one prize part) best meets my test of a voice found in this writer's work and nowhere else, sustained over a career. On public knowledge, the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid are long, deliberately patterned constructions in which memory, the body and dream form a single world, and the case rests on structure and sentence-level ambition, not on theme, politics or biography. The poetry-to-prose arc suggests development rather than a single peak, and the narrowed citation ('grounded in a poet's language') claims only what the committee's reading can support. Attribution and citation scope are unambiguous. Reservations remain: the effect depends on Romanian sentence rhythm that I judge only through translation, the poetry and early work are thinly covered, and I cannot confirm that later volumes transform rather than restate earlier motifs. I do not count the six-way convergence as merit, and I have not independently verified any source. Even so, these risks are untested, not demonstrated, so I rank the award above P000 (no award).
